name: Question 10
problem: Consider the vectors ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],$ ${a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -6\end{aligned}],$ and ${a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis $B$ of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}.$
worked_solution:
We need to find a subset of linearly independent vectors. So, we start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & -2 \\ 3 & -6 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{3}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $3$rd columns are pivot columns, while the $2$nd column is a non-pivot column.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the *original matrix*, not from the reduced one.

The $1$st and $3$rd columns from the original matrix are ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{3}.$ So, a basis of $S$ is ${{a}_{1},{a}_{3}},$ that is to say, 

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Question 10
?

Consider the vectors a1=[−23], a2=[4−6], and a3=[−2−3]. Find a basis B of Span{a1,a2,a3}.

a
B={[−23]}
b
B={[−23],[−2−3]}
c
B={[−46]}
d
B={[−23],[−46]}
e
B={[−4−6],[−2−3]}
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to find a subset of linearly independent vectors. So, we start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

A=[−24−23−6−3]R2:=R2+32R1∼[−24−200−6]

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the 1st and 3rd columns are pivot columns, while the 2nd column is a non-pivot column.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the original matrix, not from the reduced one.

The 1st and 3rd columns from the original matrix are a1 and a3. So, a basis of S is {a1,a3}, that is to say,

B={[−23],[−2−3]}.
